query: How does resolution time vary across issue themes, channel, and priority?

per_column.name: issue_theme
per_column.rationale: Directly provides the 'issue theme' axis the query requires for grouping resolution time. Categorizations are well-grounded in source text (billing, SSO/auth, performance outage, feature request). Minor imprecision: CS-0003 labeled 'performance' when it is more an outage, but still a defensible reading.

per_column.name: urgency_and_blocker_status
per_column.rationale: Adds a blocker/urgency axis distinct from the original 'priority' column, offering a genuine new dimension to model resolution time against. Values are soundly inferred from text (outage, revenue risk, enhancement-only, user friction). Partially overlaps conceptually with priority but is derived from description content, not redundant.

per_column.name: issue_type
per_column.rationale: Provides a finer taxonomy (bug vs feature vs outage vs billing error) that partially overlaps with issue_theme but adds a bug/request/error distinction useful for analysis. Grounded well, though CS-0002 labeled 'bug_functionality' when it is arguably an auth/session issue, a slight categorisation mismatch. Some redundancy with issue_theme lowers usefulness modestly.

judge.rationale: All three columns supply grounded, query-relevant axes (theme, urgency/blocker, type) for analyzing resolution time. issue_theme is the strongest; issue_type overlaps somewhat with issue_theme but still adds a bug/request/error lens. Values across the row samples are sound readings of the source text with only minor debatable categorisations and no invented facts.
